Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Customer instance, OAuth client in their registry (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Composio lists ServiceNow under 'Bring your own OAuth app', so you must supply your own client ID and secret in a custom auth config.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you need an OAuth client from the ServiceNow instance's application registry, and supply its client ID and secret to Composio.
reasons: Composio has no managed app for ServiceNow
Each ServiceNow instance holds its own OAuth client records
Your own app shows your name on the consent screen, not Composio's

prerequisites.title: Admin access on the ServiceNow instance
prerequisites.detail: Managing OAuth needs the security_admin role; creating a JWT endpoint needs admin. For customer instances, their admin must do or approve this.

prerequisites.title: Build Partner Program membership
prerequisites.detail: Required before you can list an app on the ServiceNow Store.

prerequisites.title: Valid (not self-signed) TLS certificate
prerequisites.detail: The OAuth client will not connect to endpoints using self-signed certificates.

steps.title: Get admin access to the instance
steps.detail: Use an account with security_admin on your own instance, or ask the customer's admin to do the next step.
steps.done_when: You can open System OAuth > Application Registry.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Copy the callback URL shown in the Composio dashboard for the ServiceNow auth config.

steps.title: Create OAuth client in Application Registry
steps.detail: Create an endpoint for external clients; the instance generates a client ID and secret. Enter the redirect URL.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret exist on the record.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Through Composio's API, create a custom auth config for the servicenow toolkit with the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Each user logs in and allows access
steps.detail: The end user must be logged into the instance and click Allow on the consent page.
steps.done_when: A connected account is created for the user.

steps.title: Join the Build Partner Program
steps.detail: Complete enrollment with company and legal details; this is required before listing.

steps.title: Submit app for Store certification
steps.detail: Submit the app and listing, with documentation and branding that follow guidelines.

steps.title: Wait for certification
steps.detail: Typically 3-5 weeks from submission to ready for publishing, depending on app size and iteration speed.

traps.title: The OAuth client must be registered manually in the
traps.detail: The OAuth client must be registered manually in the OpenID Connect provider as a first step; the page describes no automatic or dynamic client registration.

traps.title: No managed app in Composio
traps.detail: Composio does not supply an OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you cannot prototype with a managed one.

traps.title: OAuth client lives in each customer instance
traps.detail: The client ID and secret are generated by the specific instance, so each customer's admin must set one up.

traps.title: Self-signed certificates fail
traps.detail: The OAuth client will not connect to endpoints with self-signed certificates.

traps.title: Recertification
traps.detail: Store apps can require recertification, and you must stay within n-3 releases.

blockers.symptom: You cannot see System OAuth or Application Registry
blockers.what_it_means: Your account lacks the role needed to manage OAuth.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask an instance admin for the security_admin role, or have them create the client.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request to the admin listing the exact steps.

evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes may not include everything needed, for example write access to a specific Google API, so custom scopes may require the developer's own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of a toolkit, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio."
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available, and the page recommends switching to a custom auth config for production so users see the developer's app name.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The former, 1-2 days. Full reviews I've seen taken up to 7 days depending on what checks are required
evidence.answer: A developer-forum reply (Kieran Anson, a community member, not an official source) reports Store review waits of 1-2 days for a family release revalidation with no code change, and up to 7 days for full reviews. This concerns Store app upgrades, not OAuth app registration.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Certification, from design complete and submission for certification to ready for publishing on the store, typically requires 3-5 weeks.
evidence.answer: ServiceNow's published guide (dated 2023-02-14) says Store certification typically takes 3-5 weeks from design complete and submission to ready for publishing. It can be faster or longer depending on app size, documentation and iteration speed. This applies to Store listing certification, not OAuth app setup.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: In addition to the initial certification, ServiceNow Store apps can require recertification.
evidence.answer: Store apps can require recertification after initial certification. The guide links separate pages on recertification for new releases and for code changes, which were not opened, so trigger details are unverified.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Yes. We require you stay current (n-3) with our releases.
evidence.answer: Ongoing obligation: Technology Partners must stay current within n-3 ServiceNow releases, which drives recertification. No fixed yearly review cycle or waiver was found.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Note that you must be a Build Partner to list an application on the ServiceNow Store.
evidence.answer: Eligibility rule: listing on the ServiceNow Store requires Build Partner Program membership. This is a gate, not a user-count threshold.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: While we don't advise partners to compete, we won't block it.
evidence.answer: No hard ban on competing with core ServiceNow functionality; ServiceNow discourages it but does not block it.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Certification ensures that the app introduces the least amount of risk into the customer instance as possible and that the Store listing is accurate and adheres to branding guidelines.
evidence.answer: Use restriction: the Store listing is reviewed for accuracy and adherence to ServiceNow branding guidelines.
